purpose: How an office coffee and water service operator measures what each stop on the route actually earns once product cost, service minutes and drive time are charged against it, diagnoses whether a weak stop is failing on consumption volume or on service time, reprices consumables honestly when supplier costs move, holds accounts through reliability and run-out prevention rather than through lock-in, and grows the book by expanding only into categories a measured account will genuinely pull - while keeping route density, obligation classes and concentration risk in view.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the operator runs an established office coffee and water service with placed equipment and a recurring consumables route, so the accounts discussed here are already installed and being served

every money quantity in this KB - stop contribution, markup, delivery minimum, credit, book value - is a mechanism the operator computes from their own delivery tickets, supplier invoices and route timings, never a market figure quoted from memory or an industry rule of thumb

service minutes, drive minutes and product draw are all measurable by the operator at ordinary effort; where they are not being measured, the first work is to start measuring rather than to estimate harder

food handling, sanitation, potable-water, weights-and-measures and unattended-retail obligations differ by jurisdiction and change over time; each appears here as an obligation class to verify with the responsible authority, never as a stated requirement
retention is earned by reliability and honest pricing; contractual lock-in is treated as a weak substitute that hides a failing stop rather than fixing it
exclusions: office segmentation, prospecting, tasting and free-trial acquisition plays, proposal design and the place-versus-rent-versus-sell decision for a new account - the market targeting and account acquisition KB owns all of it

brewer and water-system model selection, physical placement, water-line and drainage work, sanitation execution, consumables catalog construction, par-level mechanics, stockroom and van inventory, and the design of the route schedule and cleaning cadence - owned by the equipment placement and route logistics KB

invented specific figures of any kind: no stated per-cup prices, markup percentages, contribution margins, churn rates, spoilage rates, route-day stop counts or account-book multiples; every such quantity appears only as a mechanism for computing it from the operator's own records

assertions about what any specific food-handling, sanitation, backflow, weights-and-measures or unattended-retail rule requires in a named jurisdiction; obligation classes are named and flagged for local verification instead
personalized legal, tax, accounting, financial or insurance advice, and the drafting or interpretation of any specific service agreement, lease or asset-purchase contract
claims about the health effects of tap water, filtration, caffeine or any beverage, and every fear-based retention or expansion tactic built on such claims

pressuring an account into inventory it does not consume, stealth pack-size reduction, undisclosed surcharges, and any repricing move the operator would not be willing to state plainly to the client in writing

competency_questions.question: Which stops on my route actually make money once product cost, service minutes and drive time are charged against them, and which ones are being carried by the rest of the route?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STOP_ECONOMIC_UNIT fixes the stop as the unit of account and STOP_CONTRIBUTION_MECHANISM states the full chain from delivered product and price down to a per-stop contribution, with every input traceable to the operator's own tickets and timings

competency_questions.question: How do I measure what an account really draws and how long it really takes to serve, instead of guessing from the invoice total?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONSUMPTION_DRAW_MEASUREMENT defines per-visit draw capture and separates true draw from shrink and waste, and SERVICE_TIME_LEDGER defines park-to-park minute capture including building access and paperwork time

competency_questions.question: This stop is thin - is the problem too little consumption or too much service time, and which fix does that diagnosis license?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WEAK_STOP_DIAGNOSIS forks the stop on volume versus time using measured inputs and names the distinct remedy set each branch allows, and COST_TO_SERVE_DRIVERS supplies the driver list the time branch is tested against

competency_questions.question: How is the price this account pays actually composed, and can I explain every part of it out loud without embarrassment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRICE_ARCHITECTURE decomposes the account price into product, equipment carry, service and any surcharge components and requires each component to be disclosable and defensible to the client

competency_questions.question: My supplier raised what I pay - how do I decide between absorbing it and passing it through, and how do I run the increase honestly?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COST_PASSTHROUGH_MECHANISM traces a documented input-cost move to the affected line and HONEST_REPRICE_PLAY specifies the notice, evidence, alternatives and no-stealth-shrinkflation conditions the increase must satisfy

competency_questions.question: How do I keep small accounts viable without punishing them with hidden fees or quietly padding their invoices?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DELIVERY_MINIMUM_DESIGN states the disclosed minimum-and-cadence instruments that make a small stop pay and CONCESSION_AND_CREDIT_DISCIPLINE bounds what may be given away and requires every concession to be recorded against the stop it burdens

competency_questions.question: What does a run-out actually cost me, and how do I prevent one without burying the client in inventory they resent?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STOCKOUT_INCIDENT_ECONOMICS converts a run-out into its retention and recovery cost and drives a root-caused prevention loop, while HONEST_EXPANSION_GATE and SERVICE_PROMISE_CAPACITY forbid solving it by overstocking the client or by promising a cadence the route cannot hold

competency_questions.question: How do I see an account leaving before the cancellation call comes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCOUNT_HEALTH_SIGNALS lists the observable leading indicators drawn from draw, service and billing records with the review that acts on them, and CHAMPION_CONTINUITY covers the contact-loss case that hides the other signals

competency_questions.question: A brewer is down or an order arrived wrong - what recovery restores trust, and what should that recovery be allowed to cost?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SERVICE_RECOVERY_LOOP defines the acknowledge-restore-verify sequence with an interim-service option and CONCESSION_AND_CREDIT_DISCIPLINE prices the credit against the stop's own contribution

competency_questions.question: When should I fight to save an account, and when do I exit cleanly, recover my equipment and free the route minutes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHURN_DECISION_AND_EXIT states the save-versus-release test against measured contribution and route capacity and specifies the equipment recovery and handover conduct of an honest exit

competency_questions.question: Which of my accounts are genuinely ready for water service, snacks, breakroom supplies or a micro-market, and how do I offer it without overstocking them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONEST_EXPANSION_GATE requires measured pull and disclosed terms before any category is added, EXPANSION_CATEGORY_SCREEN compares candidate categories on margin, spoilage, shrink and added service minutes, and MICRO_MARKET_CLASS_UPGRADE states the qualification test for the unattended-retail class

competency_questions.question: What new obligation classes do I trigger when I add food, refrigeration, or an unattended self-checkout market to an account?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FOOD_HANDLING_OBLIGATION_SHIFT names the obligation classes that change at each expansion step and requires written local verification with the responsible authority before the category goes live

competency_questions.question: Should I take this new stop, and what is my route and account book actually worth if I ever sell it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ROUTE_DENSITY_AND_MARGINAL_STOP states the incremental-minutes test for adding a stop and BOOK_VALUE_AND_CONCENTRATION describes book value as a mechanism built from recurring contribution quality, transferability, equipment condition and concentration rather than as any quoted multiple

competency_questions.question: On what cadence do I re-run stop economics, and what do I do with the stops the review flags?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ROUTE_ECONOMICS_REVIEW fixes the review cycle, its inputs and the triage decision each flagged stop receives, and routes each decision to the pricing, retention, expansion or exit node that owns it

glossary.definition: One scheduled service visit to one account location: the atomic unit this KB measures money and minutes against, since two accounts in one building served on one visit are one stop, and one account with two floors served separately is two.
One driver-and-van day covering a sequenced loop of stops; its total minutes are the scarce resource that every added stop, extended service call and emergency response competes for.
The quantity of product an account actually consumes in a period, measured as what left the stockroom or cabinet between visits rather than what was ordered or invoiced.

Product that leaves the account without being consumed on site - single-serve pods pocketed for home use, snacks taken without payment in an unattended market - which inflates apparent draw and quietly destroys the margin the draw seems to promise.

What a single stop leaves behind after its own product cost, its service labor at a loaded rate, its share of drive time and its equipment carry are charged against its billed revenue; the number that decides whether a stop is grown, repriced, re-cadenced or released.

The full recurring cost of keeping one account served - service minutes, drive allocation, cleaning and sanitation labor, consumable freight, equipment maintenance and any building-access overhead - as distinct from the cost of the product itself.

The account running out of a core consumable between visits, forcing staff to buy retail or go without; the single most common trigger of avoidable churn in office coffee service and the event whose root cause the retention loop exists to eliminate.

A pre-portioned fractional package of ground coffee sized for one brew cycle; its yield per pack is what converts a cup-level consumption estimate into the unit count that appears on a delivery ticket.

A plumbed, filtered water dispenser that replaces delivered bottles; it shifts the account's recurring line from bottle deliveries to filter changes and sanitization visits, changing both the revenue shape and the service-minute shape of the stop.

An unattended self-checkout breakroom store with open racks, coolers and a payment kiosk; a distinct service class from coffee service because it introduces inventory shrink, date-coded perishable stock, planogram maintenance and a different set of local obligations.

nodes.definition: Fix the stop - one scheduled visit to one serviceable location - as the unit every dollar and every minute in this KB is charged to, and write down the rules that decide what counts as one stop. Revenue is assigned to the stop that delivered the product, not to the customer name on the invoice, so a three-floor tenant served on three separate visits is three stops and two small firms sharing a suite door served together are one. Equipment carry travels with the stop that holds the machine, not with the corporate account, so a placed brewer sitting in a satellite office shows up in that satellite's economics. Costs that cannot be honestly attributed to a single stop - the van payment, insurance, the warehouse - are held in a route-level pool and allocated by a stated rule, and the rule is written once rather than re-invented each time a number is questioned. Without this frame every later measurement argues about its own denominator, and a profitable account and an unprofitable location hide inside the same customer record.

included: what counts as one stop and how multi-location and shared-suite cases are split
which revenue and which costs attach to a stop versus the route pool
the written allocation rule for route-level costs
excluded: the sequencing and scheduling of stops into a loop, which the route logistics KB owns
the acquisition-stage decision to pursue the location at all
company-level accounting, tax treatment and depreciation policy

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a stop definition or allocation rule change that moves several stops across the break-even line without any real-world change at those accounts

pros.claim: Charging money and minutes to a visit rather than to a customer name exposes losing locations that a healthy parent account is subsidizing
pros.example: a law firm whose main floor pays well while its two-person satellite office consumes a full visit for a handful of frac packs

pros.claim: A written allocation rule ends the recurring argument about whether a stop is really unprofitable and lets the same number be defended twice
pros.example: van and insurance cost spread across serviced stops by a stated rule rather than re-argued every time a stop is questioned

cons.claim: Stop-level attribution can make a strategically valuable location look like a loser when its real value is the relationship that feeds the profitable sites
cons.example: an executive suite that consumes almost nothing but is where the facilities director who controls four other buildings actually sits

cons.claim: Any allocation of shared route cost is a convention, so a stop near the break-even line can be argued either side of it by changing the convention
cons.example: spreading warehouse cost evenly per stop versus by delivered volume moving the same small stop from thin to negative

failure_modes: measuring profitability per customer so a losing satellite location stays invisible inside a healthy account total
leaving route-level costs entirely unallocated so every stop looks profitable and the route as a whole does not
changing the allocation rule mid-analysis to reach a conclusion someone already wanted
attributing equipment carry to head office while the machine and its maintenance burden sit somewhere else
acceptance_tests: the rule that turns locations, tenants and floors into stops is written down and applied identically to every account on the route
each stop record names which revenue lines and which cost lines attach to it and which pooled costs are allocated to it by which rule
re-running the same period with the same rule reproduces the same per-stop numbers
revisit_triggers: an account adds, merges or moves a location and the stop split no longer matches how the visit is actually run
route-level costs change materially in shape, for example a second van or a new warehouse arrangement
a triage decision hinges entirely on the allocation convention rather than on the stop itself

nodes.definition: Measure what a stop actually costs in minutes, park to park, instead of assuming the scheduled service time. The clock starts when the van stops and ends when it rolls, so it captures the loading-dock wait, the visitor badge and elevator ride, the walk with a hand truck, the brewer clean and descale, the restock and rotation, the water-cooler sanitization, the ten minutes the office manager spends chatting about an invoice, and the paperwork or signature at the end. Minutes are recorded per visit for a run of visits rather than once, because a single timed visit flatters or damns a stop unfairly - the pattern is what matters. Drive minutes between stops are recorded separately and belong to the sequence, not to the stop, which is why they are allocated rather than charged directly. The ledger is the only honest input to any cost-to-serve conversation, and it is also the fastest source of surprises: the stops that hurt are usually not the ones the driver complains about.

included: park-to-park minute capture per visit across a run of visits
the named categories that consume the minutes, including access, service, restock and client conversation
separating drive minutes from stop minutes for later allocation
excluded: designing the service and cleaning cadence itself, which the route logistics KB owns
route sequencing and van loading order
driver performance management and compensation design

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a run of newly timed visits whose pattern differs materially from the minutes currently on file for that stop

pros.claim: Measured minutes relocate the blame for a thin stop from the product to the access and handling burden that actually eats the day
pros.example: a downtown tower stop whose service work is short but whose dock check-in and freight-elevator wait doubles the visit

pros.claim: A run of timed visits distinguishes a genuinely slow stop from a bad day, so decisions are not made on one anecdote
pros.example: a stop that ran long only on the week a new machine was installed reverting to normal once the pattern is visible

cons.claim: Timing every visit adds friction for the driver and invites gaming if the numbers are used punitively rather than diagnostically
cons.example: visits recorded as shorter than they were once the driver believes long stops will be blamed on them

cons.claim: Client conversation time is real cost but also real retention work, so charging it purely as waste mismeasures its value
cons.example: the fifteen minutes with the office manager that surfaces an upcoming headcount change worth more than the minutes cost

failure_modes: using scheduled service time instead of measured park-to-park time and never seeing access overhead
timing a single visit and generalizing from it
folding drive minutes into stop minutes so nearby and distant stops look identical
treating the ledger as a driver scorecard, which corrupts the data it depends on
acceptance_tests: each stop carries measured park-to-park minutes from multiple visits, not one, with the date of each observation
access and waiting time is recorded as its own category and is visible separately from hands-on service time
drive minutes are held separately from stop minutes and are never charged directly to a single stop
revisit_triggers: a building changes its vendor access, dock or badging process
the equipment at the stop changes class, altering the cleaning and restock work
a driver change alters the measured pattern for the same stops

nodes.definition: Establish what each account actually consumes between visits, measured as the product that left the cabinet rather than the product that appeared on an order. The mechanism is a per-visit count: what was left from last visit, plus what was delivered, minus what is on the shelf now, equals draw for the interval - recorded per item class, because coffee, creamer, cups and water behave differently and an account can be growing in one and collapsing in another. Draw is then normalized to the interval length and to the days the office was actually occupied, so a holiday week or a shutdown does not read as decline. Apparent draw must be split from shrink and waste before it is trusted: pods leaving in handbags, a machine wasting product through a mis-set grind, and a case stored in a damp cupboard all consume product without earning a satisfied user. This measured series is the input that pricing, expansion, stock-out prevention and health monitoring all read from, which is why it must be a count and never an estimate carried forward from the original proposal.

included: the on-hand plus delivered minus remaining count per item class
normalization for interval length and actual office occupancy
separating true consumption from shrink and waste before the series is trusted
excluded: setting par levels and order quantities from the series, which the route logistics KB owns
the pre-sale consumption estimate used to qualify a prospect, which the acquisition KB owns
inventory accounting for the warehouse and van

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: two consecutive counted intervals whose draw sits outside the account's established band, or a shrink investigation that reclassifies part of the series

pros.claim: A counted series turns every downstream money decision into evidence rather than assertion, including the ones the client will push back on
pros.example: answering a client who says they are being over-delivered with their own counted draw across recent visits

pros.claim: Splitting draw by item class exposes silent substitution long before the account total moves
pros.example: coffee volume holding steady while creamer and cup counts fall because staff started bringing their own drinks

cons.claim: Counting at every visit adds minutes to every stop, which is exactly the cost the economics is trying to control
cons.example: a multi-cabinet floor where a full count adds meaningful time to a visit that was already long

cons.claim: Shrink is hard to isolate without accusing anyone, so the series can silently overstate genuine consumption for a long time
cons.example: single-serve pod counts that look like enthusiastic adoption and are partly stock walking home

failure_modes: treating invoiced quantity as consumption and never noticing a cupboard full of unopened stock
comparing raw intervals of different length or across a holiday shutdown and calling the difference a trend
aggregating all items into one number so a collapsing category hides inside a stable total
reading shrink as growth and increasing the standing order on the strength of it
acceptance_tests: every account has a draw series per item class built from counts at consecutive visits, each dated
the series is normalized for interval length and for known occupancy gaps before any trend is read from it
each account record states whether shrink or waste has been investigated for the item classes where apparent draw jumped
revisit_triggers: measured draw moves outside the band the account has been running in for more than one interval
the account changes headcount, in-office days or shift pattern
a new item class or brewing format is introduced, breaking comparability of the series

nodes.definition: Enumerate the specific drivers that make one account expensive to serve and another cheap, so that a thin stop can be attacked at its cause rather than repriced blindly. The recurring drivers in office coffee and water service are visit frequency, the physical access path from parking to breakroom, building vendor requirements such as badging and dock scheduling, the equipment class in place and the cleaning and descaling burden it carries, the number of separate delivery points inside one location, the fragility and freight weight of what is delivered, water-system work such as filter changes and sanitization, and the administrative drag of the account's own billing and approval process. Each driver is recorded per account as an observable fact rather than an impression, and each carries a note about whether the operator can change it, the client can change it, or nobody can. That last distinction is what makes the list useful: a stop expensive for a driver the client controls is a conversation, a stop expensive for a driver nobody controls is a pricing or exit decision.

included: the named recurring drivers of cost at an installed account
per-account recording of each driver as an observable fact
who can change each driver: operator, client or nobody
excluded: designing the cleaning cadence or selecting equipment to reduce those drivers, which the placement and logistics KB owns
vehicle and warehouse cost structure at company level
the pricing response itself, which the pricing nodes own

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a building, tenancy or equipment change at an account, or measured minutes that move without a corresponding driver change

pros.claim: Naming the driver converts a vague complaint about a hard account into a specific, negotiable item
pros.example: identifying that a single locked-storeroom key handover, not the service itself, is what stretches a visit

pros.claim: Tagging who controls each driver prevents wasted effort on costs the operator cannot move
pros.example: accepting a fixed building dock window as unchangeable and pricing for it instead of fighting it every week

cons.claim: Drivers interact, so removing one rarely delivers the full saving the list implies
cons.example: moving to a delivery point closer to the door while the badge queue continues to absorb the time saved

cons.claim: A driver list can harden into a stereotype about a class of building and stop being re-observed
cons.example: assuming every high-rise stop carries dock overhead when one tenant has ground-floor street access

failure_modes: treating cost to serve as a single number per stop with no attribution to any driver
recording impressions from the driver's memory rather than observed facts
ignoring the administrative drag of an account that requires a purchase order for every delivery
never revisiting the list after the building, tenancy or equipment changes
acceptance_tests: each served account carries a driver list with observed facts, not adjectives, behind each entry
each driver is tagged with who can change it and what the change would require
the drivers named for a stop are consistent with that stop's measured minutes rather than contradicted by them
revisit_triggers: building management changes vendor access, insurance or scheduling requirements
the account moves, adds a delivery point or changes equipment class
measured minutes shift with no change in any recorded driver, indicating a missing driver

nodes.definition: State, as an explicit chain the operator can run on their own records, how a stop's billed revenue becomes the contribution it leaves behind. Start from what the account was actually billed for the period, including consumables, any disclosed service or delivery component and any equipment rental line. Subtract landed product cost for what was delivered, taken from supplier invoices with freight included rather than from a list price. Subtract service labor as measured minutes at a loaded hourly rate the operator computes from their own payroll cost, not a wage rate. Subtract the stop's allocated share of drive time and route-level cost under the rule fixed in the stop-unit frame. Subtract equipment carry - the periodic cost of the machine sitting there, however it was funded, plus its maintenance history. Subtract credits, spoilage and write-offs charged to this stop. What remains is stop contribution for the period, and it is stated as a level and as a trend, never as a single flattering snapshot. No step of the chain may use a remembered industry figure; where an input is not measured, the chain is run as a band with the missing input widened rather than filled with a plausible number.

included: the ordered chain from billed revenue to stop contribution
the source each input must come from in the operator's own records
expressing the result as a level and trend, with bands where an input is unmeasured
excluded: company-level profit and loss, overhead recovery and tax treatment
the decision of what to do about a weak result, which belongs to diagnosis and triage
any benchmark comparison against other operators' margins

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in landed cost, loaded labor rate or allocation rule, or a period whose recomputed contribution contradicts the prior trend for several stops at once

pros.claim: One stated chain makes every stop comparable and every disagreement resolvable at a specific line rather than as a clash of opinions
pros.example: settling whether a stop is weak by pointing at its landed product cost line instead of arguing about the account overall

pros.claim: Charging equipment carry to the stop stops placed machines from becoming invisible free assets that quietly consume the route's profit
pros.example: a single-serve brewer placed years ago in an account whose draw never justified it still absorbing maintenance visits

cons.claim: The chain is only as honest as its weakest input, and a wrong loaded labor rate moves every stop at once in the same direction
cons.example: a loaded rate that omits vehicle and benefits cost making the whole route look healthier than it is

cons.claim: Period contribution is noisy for accounts that order in bursts, so a single period can misclassify a fine stop
cons.example: an office that takes a large delivery before a shutdown and nothing after, splitting one cycle across two periods

failure_modes: using list product cost instead of landed cost with freight and thereby overstating contribution on every heavy item
charging labor at a wage rate rather than a loaded rate
omitting equipment carry so placed machines look free
judging a stop from one period rather than a trend, especially for burst-ordering accounts
quietly plugging an unmeasured input with a comfortable number instead of widening the band
acceptance_tests: every input in the chain names the record it comes from: supplier invoice, delivery ticket, timing ledger, payroll or the allocation rule
the loaded labor rate is documented, dated and applied identically across all stops in the same run
each stop's result is presented as a trend across several periods with the burst-ordering cases flagged
any unmeasured input appears as a widened band rather than as a point value
revisit_triggers: supplier pricing, freight terms or the loaded labor rate changes
the allocation rule for route-level cost is amended
a stop's contribution swings across the break-even line between consecutive periods

nodes.definition: Take every stop the contribution chain flags as thin or negative and force it down one of two branches before any remedy is chosen, because the remedies are mutually exclusive and applying the wrong one makes the stop worse. The volume branch holds stops where measured draw is too small to carry any reasonable visit: the office is small, hybrid attendance gutted the demand, or the placed format produces few billable units. Its licensed remedies are lengthening the interval between visits, consolidating with a neighbouring stop, right-sizing the format, honestly growing draw where real demand exists, or applying a disclosed delivery minimum. The time branch holds stops whose draw is respectable but whose minutes are consumed by access, cleaning burden, multiple delivery points or administrative drag. Its licensed remedies are attacking the specific driver, renegotiating the access or delivery point with the client, changing equipment class, or pricing the burden openly. Stops failing on both branches are marked for the triage and exit path rather than for another round of tinkering, and the diagnosis is recorded with the evidence that placed the stop in its branch.

included: the volume-versus-time fork and the evidence that assigns a stop to a branch
the remedy set each branch licenses and the ones it forbids
marking dual-failure stops for triage rather than repair
excluded: executing the price change, which the pricing nodes own
designing the new service cadence, which the logistics KB owns
the final keep-or-release decision, which the churn and exit node owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a remedy whose measured outcome contradicts the branch it was chosen from, indicating the fork was called wrong

pros.claim: Forking before remedy stops the most common wasted move: repricing a stop whose problem was never price
pros.example: a well-consuming account made thin purely by a freight-elevator wait, where a price increase would only add churn risk to a fixable access problem

pros.claim: Recording the branch and its evidence makes the later review able to check whether the remedy worked on the cause it was aimed at
pros.example: an interval change on a low-volume stop reviewed against that stop's own draw series rather than against a general impression

cons.claim: Real stops often sit near the fork with modest weakness on both sides, and forcing a branch can oversimplify the case
cons.example: a small suburban office with mildly thin draw and a mildly awkward delivery path where neither remedy alone changes much

cons.claim: The diagnosis depends entirely on upstream measurement quality, so a stop can be branched confidently on bad minutes or unadjusted shrink
cons.example: branching a stop to volume because apparent draw fell, when the fall was shrink being curtailed rather than demand declining

failure_modes: jumping to a price increase as the universal remedy for every thin stop
cutting cadence on a time-branch stop, which reduces revenue while leaving the minute burden untouched
leaving dual-failure stops in permanent repair attempts instead of routing them to triage
diagnosing from the driver's opinion rather than from the measured series
acceptance_tests: every flagged stop carries a branch assignment with the specific measured evidence that placed it there
the remedy applied to each stop comes from the set its branch licenses, and any exception is written down with its reason
dual-failure stops are routed to triage rather than assigned another remedy round
revisit_triggers: a remedy is applied and the next period's contribution does not move in the direction the branch predicted
the account's headcount, occupancy pattern or building access changes
an upstream measurement correction reclassifies the stop's draw or minutes

nodes.definition: Decide and write down what the account is actually paying for, component by component, so that every later increase, credit or comparison has a structure to move within. The components available to an office coffee and water operator are the consumable line itself, the carry for equipment placed at no upfront charge to the client, a disclosed service or delivery component where the visit work is real and priced, any rental line where equipment is rented rather than placed, and a surcharge line where an input such as freight genuinely moves. The architecture decision is how much of the equipment and service cost is recovered inside the product price versus shown separately: recovery inside the product price is simple and familiar to clients but silently penalizes light consumers and makes a later increase look arbitrary, while separate lines are transparent and defensible but expose the operator to line-by-line shopping. Whichever structure is chosen, the binding rule is that the operator must be willing to state every component out loud to the client, and no cost may be recovered by a mechanism the client would feel deceived to discover.

included: the component set the account price is built from
the recover-inside-product versus show-separately decision and its consequences
the disclosure rule every component must satisfy
excluded: the initial proposal pricing offered to win the account, which the acquisition KB owns
catalog construction and item selection, which the logistics KB owns
drafting or interpreting the contractual price terms of any specific agreement

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a documented input-cost move, a client dispute over a line, or an equipment change that alters what the carry component represents

pros.claim: A component structure lets an increase be attached to the component that actually moved instead of applied as a blanket raise
pros.example: raising only the coffee line when green and freight costs move while leaving the service component untouched

pros.claim: Separately shown equipment carry makes a light-consuming account see the real cost of the machine it insisted on, which turns a hidden loss into an honest conversation
pros.example: a small office with a bean-to-cup machine seeing the carry line and choosing a simpler brewer instead

cons.claim: Unbundled lines invite the client to shop each line against a retail price that carries no service, which can lose an account that was fairly priced overall
cons.example: a client comparing the coffee line alone with a warehouse-club shelf price while ignoring the machine and the visits

cons.claim: Recovering everything inside the product price is simpler to sell but makes light users subsidize heavy ones and leaves increases looking unexplained
cons.example: a low-draw account paying a product price inflated by equipment recovery it cannot see and resenting the next increase

failure_modes: burying equipment and service cost in the product price and then being unable to justify an increase
inventing a fee with a vague name that the operator would not defend in a meeting
changing the architecture per account until no two accounts can be compared or repriced consistently
quoting a component against a competitor's differently-composed price without saying what each includes
acceptance_tests: each account's price is expressed as named components whose sum is the invoice, with no unexplained residual
every component has a plain-language justification the operator has actually stated to the client, in writing
the same architecture rules are applied across accounts, and any deviation is recorded with its reason
revisit_triggers: an input cost moves enough to be visible in the contribution chain
a client challenges a line as unexplained or compares it to a retail price
the equipment at the account is replaced or its funding basis changes

nodes.definition: Build the trace that connects a movement in what the operator pays to the specific price component it should affect, so that an increase is an arithmetic consequence rather than an opportunistic act. The inputs that move in this business are green and roasted coffee cost, freight and fuel, packaging, dairy and non-dairy creamer, paper goods, filters and cartridges, and the labor rate inside the service component. For each, the trace names the document that evidences the move - the supplier invoice or notice, dated - the item classes it touches, and the share of the affected line that input represents, because a move in a small input should not be allowed to justify a large change on the whole invoice. The mechanism also produces the absorb decision: a small, plausibly temporary move on an account with healthy contribution is absorbed and logged, while a durable move or a move on a stop already at the margin is passed through. What is never acceptable is passing through a cost that did not move, or passing through a move on lines it never touched.

included: the named input classes that move and the document that evidences each move
mapping a move to the specific components and item classes it touches
the absorb-versus-pass-through decision and its logging
excluded: supplier negotiation and procurement strategy
the client-facing execution of the increase, which the reprice play owns
hedging, forward buying or any financial instrument advice

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new dated supplier notice, or an absorbed move that persists past the date it was set to be re-examined

pros.claim: A documented trace lets the operator answer the client's first question - why - with a specific dated cause instead of a general one
pros.example: showing that a named consumable's landed cost moved on a dated supplier notice affecting only that item class

pros.claim: Requiring the trace prevents the slow habit of raising everything when only one input moved
pros.example: leaving cups, filters and the service component untouched when only the coffee line was affected

cons.claim: Tracing every move takes work that a small operator may skip precisely when costs are moving fastest and time is shortest
cons.example: several supplier notices landing in the same month while the route is short-handed

cons.claim: Passing through every small move trains clients to expect frequent changes and makes the operator look unstable
cons.example: three small adjustments in quick succession where one considered change would have held

failure_modes: attributing an increase to costs without being able to produce the document that shows the move
spreading a move in one input across every line on the invoice
absorbing a durable increase indefinitely until the stop is quietly loss-making
forgetting that a move can go down and never passing a decrease through
acceptance_tests: every proposed change names the input that moved, the dated document evidencing it, and the item classes it touches
the absorb-or-pass decision is recorded per account with the reason and the date it should be re-examined
downward input moves are reviewed on the same trace and acted on rather than silently retained
revisit_triggers: a supplier issues a new price notice or freight terms change
an absorbed move passes its re-examination date without reversing
a stop that was healthy when a move was absorbed falls to the margin

nodes.definition: Execute a price change as a disclosed, evidenced conversation with the account rather than as a surprise on an invoice. The play has a fixed order: confirm the increase is warranted by the passthrough trace or by measured cost to serve; check the account's own health signals so the increase is not landing the week after a run-out; give notice in writing before the first affected delivery, in language a facilities manager can repeat to their own boss; state which components move and why, naming the input that moved; offer at least one genuine alternative that keeps the client's spend flat, such as a different blend, a different format, a longer interval or a smaller pack; and take the objection seriously, including the possibility that the account is right and the increase is wrong for them. Two moves are prohibited outright: reducing pack size or weight without saying so, and adding an unexplained fee line to recover an increase the operator did not want to announce. The prohibition is not squeamishness - a client who discovers either one stops believing every other number the operator has ever given them, and the account is usually lost at the discovery rather than at the increase.

included: the ordered execution of a disclosed increase, from warrant to notice to alternatives
the prohibitions on stealth pack reduction and unexplained fee lines
handling the objection, including reversing an increase that proves wrong for that account
excluded: deciding that an input cost moved, which the passthrough mechanism owns
the contractual notice terms of any specific agreement, which require the client's own legal review
acquisition-stage discounting to win a new account

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: post-increase draw and retention outcomes at the repriced accounts compared with what the play predicted

pros.claim: Written notice with a named cause and a real alternative converts most increases into a routine renewal conversation instead of a churn event
pros.example: an account that accepts the coffee line moving because it is offered a lighter-cost blend as an alternative and keeps its spend near flat

pros.claim: Refusing stealth methods protects the credibility that every other number in the relationship depends on
pros.example: a competitor's quietly shrunk pack being discovered by the client, and the disclosed operator winning the comparison on trust

cons.claim: Disclosure invites the client to shop the account at exactly the moment they are most receptive to a competitor's tasting visit
cons.example: a facilities manager using a notice letter as the trigger to solicit two rival proposals

cons.claim: Offering alternatives can trade a price increase for a mix shift that leaves contribution no better
cons.example: the client moving to a lower-cost blend whose thinner margin cancels the intended gain

failure_modes: raising prices on the invoice with no prior notice and letting the client discover it
reducing pack size or weight instead of stating an increase
timing an increase immediately after a service failure at that account
applying a blanket increase across the book without checking which stops actually needed it
refusing to reverse an increase that clearly does not fit the account's real economics
acceptance_tests: notice is in writing, dated before the first affected delivery, and names the moving input and the affected components
at least one genuine flat-spend alternative is offered and its effect on contribution is computed before it is offered
no change reduces pack size, weight or count without stating that change explicitly
the account's recent service record is checked before the notice goes out and the timing is recorded
revisit_triggers: the account responds with a competitive quote or a cancellation threat
post-increase draw falls materially, indicating the client is substituting away rather than accepting
an alternative accepted by the client changes the mix enough to alter contribution

nodes.definition: Design the disclosed instruments that let a genuinely small account stay on the route without being carried by its neighbours or gouged for being small. The instruments are a stated minimum order value per delivery, a longer service interval matched to the account's measured draw, consolidation with another tenant in the same building into one visit, a will-call or drop-ship arrangement for accounts that cannot support a visit at all, and, where the operator chooses to use one, a delivery component priced openly for the visit itself. Every instrument is chosen from the account's own measured draw and minutes, offered in advance rather than imposed after a bad month, and explained as what it is: the visit costs something and the account is too light to cover it through product alone. The design rule is that the client should be able to choose a way to stay - a longer interval or a topped-up order - rather than being handed a fee with no alternative. A minimum that exists only to generate fee revenue from clients who cannot meet it is a churn engine wearing the costume of a pricing instrument.

included: the instrument set for small stops: minimums, longer intervals, consolidation, will-call, priced visits
choosing an instrument from measured draw and minutes and disclosing it in advance
requiring that the client has a way to comply rather than only a way to be charged
excluded: par-level and order-quantity mechanics, owned by the logistics KB
the decision to accept a small account in the first place, owned by the acquisition KB
the exit decision when no instrument makes the stop work, owned by the churn and exit node

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: observed over-ordering, stale stock or run-outs at accounts operating under a minimum or a stretched interval

pros.claim: A disclosed minimum with a compliance path keeps small accounts that would otherwise have to be dropped, and turns their order pattern into something the route can serve
pros.example: a small design studio consolidating to a larger, less frequent order and remaining a viable stop

pros.claim: Building-level consolidation converts several unviable stops into one healthy one without raising anyone's price
pros.example: three small tenants in one building agreeing to a shared delivery point and one visit

cons.claim: Minimums push clients to over-order to clear the threshold, producing stale product and the resentment that follows
cons.example: an office adding cases it will not drink for months to avoid a fee, then finding stale stock at the back of the cupboard

cons.claim: Longer intervals raise run-out risk exactly at the accounts least able to absorb one
cons.example: a stretched interval at a small office whose consumption spikes during a hiring month

failure_modes: imposing a minimum retroactively on an account that was never told
setting a minimum from a general policy rather than from the stop's own measured economics
using a fee where a longer interval would have solved the problem without cost to anyone
letting minimum-clearing orders create stale inventory the client will eventually blame the operator for
acceptance_tests: each small-stop instrument is chosen from that stop's measured draw and minutes, and the working is recorded
the instrument is communicated in writing before it takes effect, with the compliance alternative stated
accounts subject to a minimum are checked for over-ordering and stale stock at subsequent visits
revisit_triggers: the account's draw grows or falls out of the band the instrument was designed for
stale or unopened stock is observed at an account subject to a minimum
a consolidation partner in the same building leaves or changes its schedule

nodes.definition: Govern everything the operator gives away - service credits for a failure, free product to smooth an increase, a waived minimum, an extra machine at no charge, a retention discount offered under a cancellation threat - by recording it against the stop that bears it and testing it against that stop's own contribution. The discipline has three parts. First, every concession is written to the account record with its cause, its value at landed cost, and an end date, because concessions with no end date become the permanent price. Second, a concession offered to fix a failure the operator caused is treated differently from a concession offered to buy retention: the first is a cost of the failure and belongs in the service recovery loop, the second is a price change wearing a temporary label and must be judged as one. Third, the cumulative concession load per stop is reviewed, since a stop can pass every individual test and still be given away one small kindness at a time. A concession that cannot be defended out loud alongside what other accounts pay is not a concession; it is an undisclosed price the operator has quietly agreed to.

included: recording every giveaway with cause, landed value and end date
separating failure-recovery credits from retention concessions
reviewing cumulative concession load per stop
excluded: the technical response to a service failure itself, owned by the recovery loop
the decision to leave the account, owned by the churn and exit node
any credit that would constitute a rebate arrangement requiring the client's own accounting or legal review

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a concession review that finds cumulative giveaways at a stop materially changing its contribution, or a concession past its end date still running

pros.claim: Charging concessions to the stop keeps them visible in contribution, so a quietly discounted account cannot masquerade as a healthy one
pros.example: a stop whose repeated goodwill cases of coffee turn a passing contribution into a negative one once counted

pros.claim: End-dating every concession forces a deliberate decision to renew rather than an accidental permanent price
pros.example: a temporary waiver granted during a client's office move expiring and being reconsidered rather than continuing for years

cons.claim: Strict concession limits can cost an account in a moment where a fast, generous gesture would have held it
cons.example: a delayed decision on a credit after a machine failure while the client is already taking a competitor's call

cons.claim: Recording concessions in money terms understates the ones given in service, which are invisible in the ledger but real in minutes
cons.example: an unscheduled extra visit that costs route time and never appears as a credit anywhere

failure_modes: granting open-ended discounts under cancellation pressure and never revisiting them
logging credits as marketing cost at company level so the burdened stop looks healthy
treating an operator-caused failure and a retention plea as the same kind of giveaway
giving extra unscheduled service visits without counting the minutes anywhere
acceptance_tests: every concession has a written cause, a landed-cost value, an owner and an end date on the account record
concessions in service minutes are recorded alongside those in product value
each stop's contribution is computed with its concessions charged to it, not to a company-level pool
revisit_triggers: a concession reaches its end date
cumulative concessions at a stop exceed what the operator would knowingly have agreed as a price
a cancellation threat prompts a new retention offer at an account that already carries concessions

nodes.definition: Treat every run-out as a recorded incident with an economic consequence rather than as an ordinary inconvenience, because in office coffee service the empty cabinet on a Thursday morning is the event that recruits a competitor. The incident record captures which item ran out, the date and interval, what the office did about it - bought retail, went without, called - who noticed, and what the operator did in response. The cost is then assembled as a mechanism rather than a guess: the emergency drop that broke the route sequence and its minutes, any credit granted, the retail purchase the client made and now uses as a price comparison, and the standing reduction in confidence that shows up later as a competitor being invited in. Prevention is root-caused per incident and the cause is one of a small set: draw grew and the order did not, the interval was stretched too far, a delivery was missed or short, shrink drained stock invisibly, or the client changed something without telling anyone. The prohibited response is to solve every case by pushing more inventory into the client's cupboard, which converts a service failure into stale product and resentment.

included: the run-out incident record and what it must capture
assembling the incident's cost as a mechanism from route minutes, credits and confidence effects
root-cause classification and the prevention response each cause licenses
excluded: par-level and buffer stock design mechanics, owned by the logistics KB
the service cadence design itself, owned by the logistics KB
solving run-outs by overstocking the client, which the honest expansion gate forbids

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the incident series itself: a change in run-out frequency or in which root cause dominates after a prevention change

pros.claim: Recording incidents converts a vague sense that an account is unhappy into a countable pattern with a cause
pros.example: two run-outs in one quarter at the same account both traced to a stretched interval after a headcount rise

pros.claim: Costing the incident makes prevention investment arguable instead of sentimental
pros.example: an emergency drop whose broken route sequence cost more minutes than a full interval adjustment would have

cons.claim: Incident logging depends on the client telling you, and the quietest accounts under-report until they leave
cons.example: an office that simply started buying its own coffee and never mentioned the empty cabinet

cons.claim: Aggressive prevention drifts naturally toward pushing inventory, which trades a visible failure for an invisible one
cons.example: extra cases delivered after a run-out that go stale and later read to the client as over-selling

failure_modes: treating a run-out as a one-off and never recording it
responding to every run-out by increasing the standing order regardless of cause
missing shrink as a cause and repeatedly raising quantities that keep disappearing
leaving the emergency drop uncounted so the route cost of the incident stays invisible
failing to ask whether the client changed headcount or schedule before blaming the order size
acceptance_tests: each run-out has a dated incident record with item, interval, client response and root cause
the incident cost is assembled from named components including route minutes and any credit
the prevention action taken matches the recorded root cause rather than defaulting to a larger order
repeat incidents at the same account are escalated to a review of interval and draw rather than handled individually
revisit_triggers: a second incident at the same account within a review cycle
the account's draw series shows growth that the order pattern has not tracked
a shrink investigation changes the interpretation of the draw that caused the incident

nodes.definition: Keep every service promise made to an account inside what the route can actually deliver on its worst ordinary week, not its best. The promises at issue here are the visit interval, the response time for a machine failure, the emergency-delivery commitment and the window the client is told to expect the driver in. Each one is a claim on route-day minutes that are already spoken for, and each is made account by account while the capacity it consumes is shared. The work is to hold a running picture of committed minutes against available minutes per route day, including the slack that absorbs a breakdown or a sick driver, and to refuse or re-shape a promise that would consume the slack rather than accepting it and hoping. When capacity is genuinely short the honest moves are to re-sequence, to shift an account's day, to add capacity, or to tell the client plainly what can be committed - never to promise the interval that wins the moment and then miss it. A missed promise costs more than the promise ever earned, because it converts a reliability story into a reliability complaint and hands the account a reason to take a competitor's call.

included: the promise types that consume route capacity
holding committed minutes against available minutes with deliberate slack
the honest responses when a requested promise exceeds capacity
excluded: building the route schedule and sequence itself, owned by the logistics KB
hiring, vehicle and capacity investment decisions at company level
the acquisition-stage promise made to win an account, owned by the acquisition KB

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: missed-promise events and the drift between committed and available minutes on the affected route days

pros.claim: Committing against measured capacity turns reliability from an aspiration into something the operator can actually keep, which is the retention asset itself
pros.example: declining a same-day response commitment for a distant stop and offering a next-visit commitment that is always met

pros.claim: Deliberate slack absorbs the ordinary shocks that otherwise cascade into missed stops across the whole day
pros.example: a machine failure handled within the day without pushing three later stops into next week

cons.claim: Holding slack means visibly unused capacity that is tempting to sell, and the temptation is strongest exactly when the book needs growth
cons.example: filling the reserve minutes with a new stop and then having no room the first week something breaks

cons.claim: A conservative promise can lose an account to a competitor who promises more, including promises they will not keep
cons.example: a prospect choosing a rival's same-day pledge over an honest next-visit commitment

failure_modes: making per-account promises with no view of aggregate committed minutes
planning on best-case route days and having no absorption for a breakdown or absence
letting an unofficial promise from a driver become the client's expectation
keeping a promise for the loud accounts by quietly missing the quiet ones
acceptance_tests: every promise made to an account is written on the account record in the terms the client was given
committed minutes per route day are held against available minutes with a stated slack allowance
any promise that would consume the slack is escalated to a re-shape or refusal decision rather than accepted by default
revisit_triggers: a promise is missed at any account
a stop is added, removed or re-timed on a route day that was already near its committed limit
measured stop minutes drift upward across the day, eroding the slack

nodes.definition: Run the standard sequence that follows any failure the client experiences - a brewer down, a water system leaking, a wrong or short delivery, an invoice error, a missed visit - because how the failure is closed determines whether it costs the account or strengthens it. The sequence is acknowledge, restore, verify, and account for. Acknowledge means a same-working-day human response naming what happened without excuses. Restore means a defined interim that keeps the breakroom functioning while the real fix happens: a loaner machine, a pour-over setup with product, a manual dispenser, or an interim delivery. Verify means going back to confirm the fix held rather than assuming silence is satisfaction, since the next failure at the same account is far more expensive than the first. Account for means recording the failure, its cause, its minutes and any credit against the stop, so that a chronically failing machine or a chronically failing building shows up in the economics instead of hiding in goodwill. The loop is also where equipment reliability turns into an economic decision: the third failure of the same unit is a replacement question, not another service call.

included: the acknowledge-restore-verify-account sequence and its interim-service options
recording failure cause, minutes and credits against the stop
escalating a repeatedly failing unit into a replacement decision
excluded: the technical repair procedure and preventive maintenance schedule, owned by the logistics KB
warranty claims and supplier remedies, which require the operator's own contract review
the credit amount policy itself, owned by the concession discipline node

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the failure record itself: repeat causes, verification outcomes and the minutes recovery is consuming per period

pros.claim: A defined interim keeps the breakroom working during the failure, which is what the client actually cares about
pros.example: leaving a loaner brewer and product the same day while the failed machine is taken for repair

pros.claim: Verifying the fix and recording the cause converts recurring failures into a visible pattern instead of a series of forgotten calls
pros.example: a unit whose third failure in one account triggers replacement rather than another repair visit

cons.claim: Fast recovery consumes exactly the route slack that reliability depends on, so a bad week of failures degrades service everywhere
cons.example: two same-day recovery runs pushing scheduled stops into the following week

cons.claim: Generous recovery can teach an account to escalate ordinary issues, raising the cost of serving it
cons.example: a client who begins calling for immediate attendance on minor issues after a strong recovery

failure_modes: acknowledging the failure but leaving the client without any interim way to make coffee
closing the ticket when the repair is done without verifying the fix held
absorbing recovery minutes into the day without recording them against the stop
repairing the same unit repeatedly instead of escalating it to a replacement decision
letting the recovery conversation drift into blaming the client or the building
acceptance_tests: every failure has a dated record with cause, interim provided, verification date and the minutes it consumed
an interim service option is offered in every case where the client's breakroom would otherwise be out of service
units with repeated failures at the same account are escalated to a replacement decision rather than re-repaired by default
revisit_triggers: a second failure of the same type at the same account
recovery minutes in a period materially exceeding the slack allowance
a client dispute about whether a past failure was properly resolved

nodes.definition: Protect the account against the departure of the one person who cares about it. In office coffee service the relationship almost always runs through a single office manager, executive assistant or facilities coordinator who chose the service, defends it in budget season and calls when something breaks. When that person leaves, the account becomes a line item to a successor with no history and often with a mandate to cut costs, and this is one of the most common ways a perfectly well-served account is lost. The work is to know who the champion is by name and role, to have at least one other contact who has met the driver and knows how the service works, to make sure the account's value is documented in a form the client keeps rather than only in the operator's head, and to notice the departure early - a bounced email, a new name on the delivery signature, a changed approval process. When the successor appears, the response is a short, factual re-introduction that shows the account's own numbers: what is delivered, what it costs, what the equipment is, what has been fixed. Cultivating the champion is legitimate relationship work, but it stays inside the client's own gift and hospitality rules, and no personal inducement may be used to influence a purchasing decision.

included: identifying the champion and a second contact per account
early detection of a contact change and the factual re-introduction that follows
the conduct limits on cultivating a client contact
excluded: the original decision-maker mapping performed while winning the account, owned by the acquisition KB
any gift, entertainment or inducement decision that would require the client's or operator's own compliance review
the pricing response to a new manager's cost-cutting mandate, owned by the pricing nodes

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: champion turnover events and whether accounts with a documented alternate contact survived them differently from single-threaded ones

pros.claim: A second known contact keeps the account explicable when the champion leaves, which is when most avoidable churn happens
pros.example: a departing office manager's successor already knowing the driver by name and the delivery routine

pros.claim: Documenting the service in a form the client keeps means the account's value survives the memory of one person
pros.example: a one-page service summary in the client's own facilities folder listing equipment, cadence and contacts

cons.claim: Multi-threading can annoy a champion who regards the account as their domain and reads the second contact as going around them
cons.example: an office manager who takes offence at the driver introducing himself to the operations lead

cons.claim: Relationship investment is unmeasurable and can absorb service minutes that the stop economics never credits
cons.example: regular conversation time at a stop whose contribution stays thin regardless

failure_modes: knowing only one contact and discovering the departure from a cancellation email
assuming a successor understands what the service includes and why it costs what it costs
responding to a new manager's cost question with defensiveness rather than the account's own numbers
using personal inducements to hold a contact, which risks the client's own policies and the operator's reputation
acceptance_tests: every account record names the champion, their role, and at least one alternate contact who has met the service
a contact-change detection signal exists and is acted on within the current review cycle
the re-introduction pack for a successor is factual, uses the account's own numbers, and is available on short notice
revisit_triggers: any change in the named champion or the approval process
an account reorganization, move or acquisition
the alternate contact also leaving, restoring single-thread exposure

nodes.definition: Assemble the small observable signals that appear weeks before a cancellation, from records the operator already holds, so that the account is worked while it can still be saved. The signals in this business are a sustained fall in measured draw that occupancy does not explain, a shift toward the cheapest items in the catalog, run-out incidents that the client stopped reporting, calls and emails going unanswered by a previously responsive contact, a new name signing for deliveries, invoice queries where there were none, requests for a copy of the agreement or its termination terms, a competitor's brewer or water cooler appearing in another part of the office, and a client suddenly asking for itemized pricing after years of paying without question. Each signal is recorded with its date and reviewed on the account's own baseline rather than against the route average, since a quiet account has always been quiet. The output is a per-account health state that routes the account to a save action, an expansion conversation or a triage decision - and the discipline is to act on the signal rather than to wait for the certainty that only arrives with the cancellation.

included: the observable leading indicators drawn from draw, service, contact and billing records
reading each signal against the account's own baseline
routing an account by health state to save, expand or triage
excluded: the save-versus-release decision itself, owned by the churn and exit node
the expansion offer, owned by the honest expansion gate
any inference about the client's internal finances beyond what they have told the operator

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cancellations reviewed against the signals that were and were not present beforehand

pros.claim: Leading indicators buy the weeks in which a save is still possible, which a cancellation notice never does
pros.example: acting on three intervals of falling draw and an unreturned call before the competitor's tasting is scheduled

pros.claim: Using the account's own baseline avoids constant false alarms from accounts that were always low-volume
pros.example: a small firm whose steady, modest draw reads as healthy rather than as decline

cons.claim: Signals are ambiguous and a decline can be the client's own business shrinking rather than dissatisfaction, so the wrong response can insult a loyal account
cons.example: pitching a retention discount to a client whose draw fell because they laid off half the office

cons.claim: Signal monitoring can degrade into anxious over-contact, which itself annoys the account
cons.example: repeated check-in calls to a client whose only issue was a holiday shutdown

failure_modes: watching only revenue, which moves last, instead of draw and service signals, which move first
comparing an account to route averages rather than to its own history
recording signals but never assigning anyone to act on them
reading every decline as dissatisfaction and never asking the client what changed
acceptance_tests: each account carries a dated signal log and a current health state with the evidence behind it
signals are evaluated against that account's own baseline, and the baseline is stated
every account in a deteriorating state has a named next action with an owner and a date
revisit_triggers: a new signal type appears that the log does not capture
an account cancels with no prior signal recorded, indicating a blind spot
the account's occupancy or business circumstances change in a way that resets its baseline

nodes.definition: Decide, for an account in trouble or an account the economics cannot justify, whether to save it or to release it - and if released, to leave in a way that costs nothing beyond the account itself. The save test is not sentiment: it asks whether the account's contribution can plausibly reach a level the route should keep once the specific cause is fixed, whether the fix is inside the operator's control, and what the freed minutes would earn if the stop were released and the capacity used elsewhere. A save is executed as a written commitment with a review date, not as a discount handed over in a phone call. A release is executed as a planned exit: notice given in the terms of the agreement, final deliveries honored, equipment de-installed and recovered with its condition recorded, water connections properly closed off by whoever is qualified to do it, final invoicing settled without punitive extras, and the client left with enough notice and information to arrange their own alternative. The reason this conduct matters commercially is that offices talk to each other and facilities managers move between buildings; the account being released today is a reference tomorrow, and an operator who exits badly buys a reputation that outlasts the stop.

included: the save-versus-release test against contribution, controllable cause and the value of freed capacity
executing a save as a written commitment with a review date
the planned-exit conduct: notice, equipment recovery, closure and final settlement
excluded: interpreting the termination clauses of any specific agreement, which requires the client's or operator's own legal review
the technical de-installation and water disconnection procedure, owned by the logistics KB
any collections or dispute action, which is outside this KB

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: outcomes of past saves and releases: whether saved accounts reached their stated contribution and whether freed capacity was actually re-sold

pros.claim: An explicit release decision converts a slow bleed into recovered route capacity that can be sold to a better stop
pros.example: releasing a chronically negative stop and using the freed minutes to add an infill account nearby

pros.claim: A clean exit protects referrals in a market where facilities managers move between buildings and talk
pros.example: a released client later recommending the operator at their next employer because the handover was handled well

cons.claim: Releasing a stop removes a fixed revenue line immediately while the replacement demand is uncertain and slower than expected
cons.example: freed capacity sitting unsold for longer than planned after an exit

cons.claim: Exit costs are real and front-loaded: de-installation, recovery, unrecoverable equipment condition and any remaining product
cons.example: a placed machine returning damaged and unfit for the next account

failure_modes: saving every account by discount, converting a churn problem into a permanent margin problem
letting a decided release drag on for months while the stop keeps consuming minutes
abandoning equipment at a released account because recovery seemed like too much trouble
exiting with punitive final charges that turn a lost account into an active detractor
leaving a water connection or drain unclosed for someone else to discover
acceptance_tests: each save decision states the cause being fixed, the contribution it is expected to reach, and the date it will be reviewed
each release names the notice given, the equipment recovered with its recorded condition, and the closure steps completed
freed capacity from a release is explicitly assigned to a use rather than absorbed invisibly
revisit_triggers: a saved account fails to reach its stated contribution by the review date
released capacity remains unsold beyond the period assumed in the decision
an exit produces a complaint, a dispute or a lost referral

nodes.definition: Bind every attempt to sell an existing account more - another machine, water service, tea and cocoa variety, snacks, breakroom supplies, a market upgrade - to evidence that the account will actually pull it, and to terms the client can see whole before agreeing. The gate has four conditions. Pull: the demand is visible in the account's own records or in something the client has said, not inferred from the operator's need for revenue. Reliability: the core service at that account is currently sound, since expanding an account that ran out of coffee twice this quarter is selling on top of a broken promise. Right-sizing: the initial quantity and assortment are sized to measured draw with a stated plan to grow or shrink at the next visit, so the client is never left holding stock they cannot consume. Disclosure: the price of the new category, any equipment carry it adds, its minimum and the exit path from it are stated before the first delivery. The gate exists because the failure mode it prevents is specific and destructive: an operator who pushes volume into cupboards converts a customer's goodwill into resentment, and the resentment arrives later as a cancellation that also takes the coffee service with it.

included: the four gate conditions: pull, reliability, right-sizing and disclosure
sizing an initial assortment to measured draw with an explicit adjust-next-visit plan
the prohibition on volume pushed for the operator's benefit
excluded: which categories are worth adding at all, owned by the category screen
acquisition-stage proposal design for new accounts, owned by the acquisition KB
assortment and planogram construction, owned by the logistics KB

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: post-launch reviews showing whether expanded categories were consumed as predicted or left unconsumed and withdrawn

pros.claim: Requiring visible pull means expansion revenue tends to stick instead of reversing at the first stock review
pros.example: a water system added only after staff were repeatedly seen refilling bottles at a distant tap and the office asked about it

pros.claim: Right-sizing with an explicit adjustment at the next visit lets an account try a category with almost no risk of being stuck with it
pros.example: a small starter assortment of snacks reviewed at the following visit and cut back on the items nobody touched

cons.claim: Waiting for demonstrated pull leaves revenue on the table where a client would have happily accepted a suggestion
cons.example: an office that would have taken tea variety immediately but was never offered it because no pull signal existed yet

cons.claim: Small right-sized starts can under-serve a category and make it look unsuccessful when the assortment was simply too thin to be used
cons.example: a snack offering too limited to become part of anyone's routine and then withdrawn as a failure

failure_modes: loading an account with a category because the operator needs the volume this month
expanding an account that has unresolved service failures or unpaid disputes
sizing the first order from a supplier's suggested assortment rather than the account's own draw
leaving the exit path from a new category unstated so the client feels trapped
treating an unreturned suggestion as consent to deliver
acceptance_tests: each expansion has a recorded pull signal from the account's own evidence, dated and specific
the account's current reliability state is checked and recorded before the offer is made
the initial quantity is traceable to measured draw and carries a stated review-and-adjust date
the price, any added carry, the minimum and the exit path are given to the client in writing before the first delivery
revisit_triggers: the first review after a category launch shows unconsumed or expired stock
the account raises a service or billing issue after an expansion
the pull signal that justified the expansion turns out to have come from a small group that has since left

nodes.definition: Compare the candidate categories an office coffee and water operator can add to an existing stop, on the dimensions that actually decide whether they help, and sequence them so the easy compounding ones come before the demanding ones.
