The realistic ladder runs from beverage variety within the existing equipment - tea, cocoa, alternative creamers, a second blend - through point-of-use water service or filtered bottle replacement, through cold beverage and paper-goods and breakroom supplies, and only then to snack racks, refrigerated items and finally an unattended market class. Each candidate is screened on: the added service minutes per visit, the freight and handling weight it adds to the van, its margin shape as computed from the operator's own landed cost, its spoilage and date-code exposure, its shrink exposure, the equipment or fixtures it demands, the obligation classes it may trigger, and whether it deepens the reason the client keeps the operator or merely adds an item. Categories that add minutes to every visit are judged much more harshly than ones that ride along on the existing stop, because minutes are the binding constraint on the whole route.

included: the candidate category ladder and its ordering logic
the screening dimensions including minutes, weight, margin shape, spoilage, shrink and fixtures
judging categories by their effect on the binding route-minute constraint
excluded: the specific item assortment and planogram, owned by the logistics KB
the qualification test for the unattended market class specifically, owned by its own node
verifying which obligations apply locally, owned by the obligation-shift node

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured minutes, spoilage and shrink from a category after a full cycle, compared with the values the screen assumed

pros.claim: Screening on added minutes prevents a category that looks profitable per item from quietly consuming the route's capacity
pros.example: a refrigerated line that adds rotation and date-checking work to every visit on the loop

pros.claim: Sequencing from ride-along categories upward compounds revenue at almost no operational cost before any complex class is attempted
pros.example: adding tea and a second blend within the existing equipment before considering any refrigerated offering

cons.claim: A minutes-first screen is biased against categories whose real value is defensive, making the account harder for a competitor to take whole
cons.example: breakroom supplies that add handling time but make the operator the single source the office relies on

cons.claim: Spoilage and shrink exposure are hard to estimate before running a category, so the screen's hardest inputs are its weakest
cons.example: date-coded stock in a small office whose real waste rate only becomes visible after a full cycle

failure_modes: screening categories on gross margin alone and ignoring the minutes and weight they add
adopting a supplier's category program wholesale without screening it against this route's constraints
jumping the ladder to a complex class before the simple ones are working
ignoring that a category changes the van load and therefore the sequence of the whole route day
acceptance_tests: each candidate category carries a screen record covering minutes, weight, margin shape, spoilage, shrink, fixtures and obligation exposure
the ladder position of each category is stated along with what must be working before the next step is attempted
margin shape is computed from the operator's own landed cost, never from a supplier's suggested figures
revisit_triggers: a launched category's measured minutes or spoilage differ from what the screen assumed
supplier terms, freight or product availability change the margin shape of a category
route capacity changes, altering how harshly added minutes should be judged

nodes.definition: Treat the move from breakroom service to an unattended self-checkout market as a change of business class rather than as a bigger version of the same stop, and qualify an account against that reality before any fixture is ordered. The qualification questions are concrete: is the on-site population large enough and present enough days to turn stock before it dates; is the space secure and supervised enough that shrink stays inside what the category can carry; does the client accept the loss policy in writing, including who bears shrink and expired stock; is there power, network and payment connectivity for the kiosk; can the route absorb the restocking, rotation and cash-and-remote-monitoring work that a market adds to every visit; and what happens to the fixtures and the unrecovered investment if the client cancels or moves. The economics differ from coffee service in kind: capital is sunk into fixtures rather than a brewer, revenue depends on assortment and turn rather than a standing order, and losses arrive as shrink and date-outs rather than as bad debt. An account that is merely enthusiastic does not qualify; an account with the population, the supervision and the written loss terms does.

included: the qualification questions covering population, turn, shrink exposure, connectivity, route absorption and cancellation exposure
written loss and shrink terms with the client
the fixture investment and its recovery exposure
excluded: fixture selection, planogram and installation execution, owned by the logistics KB
the local obligation classes an unattended market triggers, owned by the obligation-shift node
payment processing contracts and any tax or accounting treatment, which require the operator's own professional advice

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured shrink, date-out losses and added visit minutes from an operating market compared with the qualification assumptions

pros.claim: Qualifying on population and turn before investing prevents fixtures being sunk into an account that cannot rotate perishable stock
pros.example: declining a market for a small hybrid office whose typical on-site count would leave dated stock every cycle

pros.claim: Written loss terms make shrink a shared, discussable fact instead of an argument after the first bad month
pros.example: agreeing in advance how unexplained losses are reviewed and who bears them before the market opens

cons.claim: The class carries sunk fixture cost with a real chance of an early cancellation, which is a materially different risk from a placed brewer
cons.example: a client relocating within a year of the market opening and the fixtures needing removal and refurbishment

cons.claim: Markets add recurring work of a kind the coffee route was never designed for, including rotation, kiosk issues and remote monitoring
cons.example: date-checking and planogram tidying turning a short stop into the longest one on the day

failure_modes: qualifying an account on enthusiasm and headcount on paper rather than on typical on-site presence
opening a market without written shrink and loss terms
underestimating the added visit work until the route day no longer fits
ignoring the cancellation and relocation exposure on sunk fixtures
launching before the local obligation classes have been verified
acceptance_tests: the qualification record answers every question - population and presence, turn, supervision and shrink, connectivity, route absorption, cancellation exposure - with account-specific evidence
loss, shrink and expired-stock terms are agreed in writing with the client before opening
the added visit minutes are estimated from the screen and checked against the route day's remaining capacity
the obligation-class verification for unattended retail is complete and recorded before opening
revisit_triggers: measured shrink or date-out losses exceed what the qualification assumed
the account's on-site population pattern changes
the client signals a relocation, restructuring or cancellation while fixtures remain unrecovered

nodes.definition: Recognize that moving an account from sealed shelf-stable coffee into other categories can move the operator into different regulatory classes, and re-verify locally at each step instead of assuming the coffee-service position still holds. The classes to check by name, with the responsible authority in the operator's own jurisdiction, include: retail or wholesale food-facility obligations once open, perishable or refrigerated food is supplied; date-marking, temperature control and traceability obligations for chilled and dated items; food-handler certification and sanitation obligations for staff who handle open product or clean dispensing equipment; potable-water, backflow-prevention and plumbing obligations for point-of-use water systems and ice equipment; weights-and-measures or pricing-display obligations where product is sold to consumers at a posted price; unattended-retail and payment-handling obligations for a self-checkout market; and any vendor requirements the building itself imposes, such as insurance certificates and sanitation documentation. Every one of these varies by jurisdiction and changes over time, so this node names the class and requires written verification with the responsible authority before the category goes live; it never states what any specific rule requires. The commercial reason to treat this as a gate rather than paperwork is that the discovery of an unmet obligation usually arrives with the client, and it takes the account with it.

included: the obligation classes whose applicability can change with category expansion
requiring dated written verification with the responsible authority per jurisdiction
treating verification as a gate that precedes launch
excluded: stating what any specific rule requires in any named jurisdiction
legal interpretation, permit drafting or representation before any authority
the sanitation execution procedure for equipment, owned by the logistics KB

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a written answer from a responsible authority, a building requirement, or any change in the categories the operator supplies

pros.claim: Naming the class rather than the rule keeps the guidance correct across jurisdictions and forces a real local check
pros.example: identifying that adding chilled items raises a food-facility question and verifying it with the local authority before ordering a cooler

pros.claim: Verifying before launch prevents the worst discovery path, which is the client or a building manager finding the gap first
pros.example: a building requiring documentation for a new refrigerated offering that the operator already holds

cons.claim: Verification takes calendar time and can stall an expansion the client is enthusiastic about right now
cons.example: a market launch waiting on a written answer while the client's interest cools

cons.claim: Answers can be ambiguous or informal, and an informal answer is weak protection later
cons.example: a verbal assurance by phone that nobody can produce when the question is raised again

failure_modes: assuming that because coffee service required nothing special, food or water categories require nothing special
relying on a supplier's claim that a category is compliant everywhere
verifying once and never again as the categories or the rules change
accepting an informal verbal answer and keeping no dated record of it
stating a specific requirement to a client rather than pointing them to the authority
acceptance_tests: each category change has a written list of the obligation classes it may touch and the authority responsible for each
each class is marked verified or unverified with a date and the form the answer took
no category goes live with an unverified class that could apply to it
the record states explicitly that requirements vary by jurisdiction and must be re-verified over time
revisit_triggers: a new category, item class or piece of equipment is proposed
an authority, building or client requests documentation the operator does not hold
the verification record passes the age at which the operator has decided to re-check

nodes.definition: Treat geographic density, not account count, as the engine that makes an office coffee route profitable, and test every candidate addition on its incremental effect rather than on its own revenue. The mechanism is simple and unforgiving: drive minutes between stops are pure cost that no client pays for directly, so two accounts in the same building or the same block share an approach that a distant account of equal size does not. The marginal-stop test asks what adding this stop does to the route day: the incremental drive minutes to reach it from the existing sequence, the service minutes it adds, whether it fits inside the day without displacing another stop or eroding the slack, and what it does to the loop on the days it is not served. The same test runs in reverse when a stop is released, because losing an anchor stop in a distant cluster can turn its neighbours from profitable to marginal overnight. Density also compounds in retention: a route with several accounts in one building can respond fast, cover a failure cheaply and be visible in a way a scattered route cannot.

included: the incremental test for adding or releasing a stop
density effects on drive minutes, response capability and slack
the anchor-stop dependency inside a distant cluster
excluded: route sequencing and daily dispatch, owned by the logistics KB
prospect targeting and territory definition for new business, owned by the acquisition KB
vehicle and staffing capacity investment decisions

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured drive and service minutes after an add or release, compared with the incremental estimate that justified it

pros.claim: The incremental test correctly accepts a small nearby stop and correctly rejects a larger distant one, which raw revenue comparison inverts
pros.example: adding a modest account two floors above an existing stop while declining a bigger account across town

pros.claim: Running the test in reverse before releasing a stop protects the neighbours that depended on the same trip
pros.example: recognizing that dropping the anchor account in an outlying cluster would strand two adjacent stops

cons.claim: Strict density discipline concentrates the book geographically, so a single building, campus or employer becomes a correlated exposure
cons.example: several stops in one tower all affected when the building changes vendor access rules or the anchor tenant leaves

cons.claim: Incremental logic can justify accepting many thin stops that are individually defensible and collectively fill the day with low-contribution work
cons.example: a loop packed with small nearby accounts that leaves no room for a strong stop when one appears

failure_modes: comparing a candidate stop on its own revenue instead of on its incremental minutes
adding stops until the slack that absorbs failures has quietly disappeared
releasing an anchor stop without testing what it does to its cluster
treating a distant prestige account as a marketing asset while it drains the route day
acceptance_tests: every add or release decision records incremental drive minutes, incremental service minutes and the effect on that route day's remaining slack
cluster dependencies are recorded so anchor stops are identified before any release decision
the route day's committed minutes after the change are checked against its available minutes
revisit_triggers: a stop is added or released in any cluster
measured drive or service minutes drift so that a previously accepted addition no longer fits
a building or tenant change alters the cluster's composition

nodes.definition: Understand what a route and its account book are actually worth, as a mechanism a buyer or a lender would work through, and manage the fragility that quietly discounts it. Value is built from the recurring contribution the book produces after honest cost to serve, the durability of that contribution across recent periods, the transferability of the accounts - whether agreements and equipment can be assigned and whether the relationships survive a change of operator - the geographic density that determines whether the book can be run efficiently by someone else, the condition and remaining life of the placed equipment and whether it is owned free of encumbrance, the cleanliness of the records themselves, and the concentration of the book in a few accounts, buildings or employers. Concentration is the fragility to manage actively: a book where one account or one tower carries a large share of contribution is worth less and is riskier to run, because a single tenancy decision moves the whole business. No multiple, ratio or valuation figure is asserted here; the operator computes their own contribution and durability from their own records, and any actual transaction is priced with their own professional advisers.

included: the value drivers of a route book stated as a mechanism: recurring contribution, durability, transferability, density, equipment condition, record quality
concentration by account, building and employer as an actively managed fragility
keeping the records a buyer or lender would need in the form they would need them
excluded: any stated multiple, ratio or valuation figure
the negotiation, structuring, tax or legal treatment of an actual sale, which requires the operator's own professional advisers
acquiring another operator's book, which is a separate transaction discipline

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in concentration, cluster composition or equipment inventory, or an external review by a lender or buyer that tests the records

pros.claim: Knowing the value mechanism changes daily behaviour, because the same records that raise value are the ones that run the route well
pros.example: keeping per-stop contribution and equipment condition current because both are what a buyer would examine

pros.claim: Watching concentration turns a hidden single-point failure into a managed growth target
pros.example: deliberately adding stops in a second cluster when one building's share of contribution grows uncomfortably large

cons.claim: Managing to a future sale can distort present decisions toward records and appearances rather than service
cons.example: keeping a marginal account on the book purely to preserve stop count

cons.claim: Value drivers are only partly in the operator's control, since transferability depends on agreements and relationships that may not survive a handover
cons.example: accounts whose loyalty runs to the individual driver rather than to the business

failure_modes: measuring the book by revenue rather than by contribution after honest cost to serve
letting one account or one building grow to dominate the book without a stated ceiling
keeping records so informal that the contribution cannot be demonstrated to anyone else
assuming placed equipment adds value when its age, condition and encumbrance are unknown
quoting or relying on a rule-of-thumb valuation figure heard from another operator
acceptance_tests: the book is reported as recurring contribution by stop and cluster, with its durability across recent periods visible
concentration by account, building and employer is computed and compared against a ceiling the operator has stated in advance
placed equipment is inventoried with age, condition and ownership status
no valuation figure or multiple is asserted anywhere in the record; value drivers are described as mechanisms
revisit_triggers: the largest account or building crosses the concentration ceiling
a cluster is gained or lost, changing density and durability
the operator begins to consider a sale, a loan or a partner, raising the record-quality bar

nodes.definition: Run the whole apparatus on a fixed cycle rather than when something goes wrong, and give every flagged stop a decision that leaves the review with an owner and a date. The review takes the same inputs each time: the draw series per account, the minute ledger, the current contribution per stop and its trend, the run-out and failure incident logs, the concession register, the health-signal states, the promise-versus-capacity picture per route day, and the concentration position of the book. Its output is a triage list where each flagged stop is assigned exactly one of: grow honestly, reprice through the disclosed play, re-cadence or re-instrument, fix a named cost driver, expand through the gate, or route to the save-versus-release decision. The review also checks its own inputs: which stops have stale timings, which accounts have no counted draw this cycle, which concessions have passed their end date, and which obligation verifications are aging. The cadence itself is chosen by the operator to match how fast their route changes, and the standing rule is that a decision made in the review has an owner and a review date, because a triage list nobody owns is just a list of stops everyone already worried about.

included: the fixed input set the review consumes and the single-decision triage it produces
the self-audit of stale timings, missing counts, expired concessions and aging verifications
assigning an owner and a review date to every decision
excluded: the execution of any individual remedy, which the owning node performs
financial statement preparation and reporting, which is outside this KB
the acquisition pipeline review for new business, owned by the acquisition KB

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the hit rate of prior cycles' decisions and the share of stops whose predicted movement actually occurred

pros.claim: A fixed cycle catches slow deterioration that no single event would ever surface
pros.example: three stops drifting toward marginal over several periods with no complaint, incident or cancellation to raise an alarm

pros.claim: Forcing exactly one decision per flagged stop prevents the standing list of known problems that never resolves
pros.example: a chronically thin stop finally assigned to release with a date instead of appearing on the list for the fourth cycle

cons.claim: A periodic review can be too slow for a fast-moving failure, so it must not replace event-driven response
cons.example: a run-out and a champion departure in the same week that cannot wait for the next cycle

cons.claim: Review overhead is real work for a small operator and competes directly with the route it is measuring
cons.example: a cycle skipped during a short-staffed period, leaving the next one twice as large

failure_modes: running the review on revenue reports alone without the minute ledger or incident logs
producing a triage list with no owners or dates
letting event-driven problems wait for the review cycle
skipping the input self-audit so decisions are made on stale timings and uncounted draw
assigning multiple conflicting remedies to the same stop in one cycle
acceptance_tests: each cycle consumes the full stated input set and records which inputs were stale or missing
every flagged stop leaves the review with exactly one assigned decision, an owner and a review date
decisions from the previous cycle are checked for outcome before new ones are assigned
event-driven escalations are shown to have been handled outside the cycle rather than deferred into it
revisit_triggers: a cycle is skipped or its inputs are materially incomplete
decisions from prior cycles repeatedly fail to produce the predicted movement
the route changes fast enough that the chosen cadence is visibly too slow

edges.why_related: minutes can only be recorded once it is settled what counts as one stop, otherwise a multi-floor tenant's time is attributed to whichever record happens to be open
draw is counted per serviced location, so the stop split decides which cabinet's counts belong to which record
drivers such as access path and delivery points are properties of a serviced location, which the stop definition fixes
the service labor line of the contribution chain is measured minutes at a loaded rate, and without the ledger it is a guess
landed product cost and billed volume both derive from what the account actually drew rather than from what was ordered
the driver list explains which costs belong to the stop and which are pooled, which the chain must respect to stay honest
only a computed contribution can flag a stop as thin, and the diagnosis reads the same inputs the chain used
the price components must recover the costs the contribution chain actually charges to the stop, including equipment carry
a cost move can only be traced to a component if the components exist and are defined
the play requires a documented warrant before any notice goes out, and the trace is that warrant
repricing is licensed only for stops the fork placed where price is actually the lever, not for every thin stop
a minimum or priced visit is a component of the same disclosed structure and must sit inside it rather than beside it
root-causing a run-out requires the counted draw series to show whether demand grew, the interval stretched, or stock disappeared
committed minutes can only be held against available minutes when stop minutes are measured rather than assumed
the recovery response is only deliverable if the route holds the slack the promise assumed
the incident log is one of the strongest leading indicators the health state reads, especially when incidents stop being reported
the save-or-release test needs a health state and its evidence before it can judge whether the cause is fixable
categories are only screened for accounts that have already passed the pull, reliability, sizing and disclosure conditions
the market class sits at the top of the ladder and is only considered once the screen has cleared the simpler categories
the incremental test compares a candidate's added minutes against contribution computed the same way for every existing stop
density is one of the value drivers of the book and determines whether another operator could run it efficiently
the review reads the concentration and durability position as one of its standing inputs
an unattended market may touch food-facility, unattended-retail and payment-handling obligation classes, none of which may be assumed from the coffee-service position
edges.risk_of_conflict: fixtures ordered and stock committed before a class is verified, forcing an expensive stand-down

edges.why_related: the market class is the expansion with the largest sunk cost, so the pull, reliability, sizing and disclosure conditions bind hardest there
the gate's reliability condition reads the incident log directly: an account with unresolved run-outs is not eligible for a new category
an addition that fits the map but consumes the slack the promises depend on is refused however attractive its contribution looks
credits, free product and unscheduled visits must be charged to the stop that received them or the contribution chain reports a stop that does not exist
the increase a stop needs economically often falls due exactly when the account's health signals are deteriorating, and the two pull in opposite directions
edges.resolution_rule: if the deterioration traces to an operator-caused failure, stabilize and verify the fix before any notice goes out; if it traces to the client's own occupancy or budget, proceed with the notice but lead with the flat-spend alternatives rather than the increase

edges.why_related: stretching the interval or imposing a minimum is how a small stop is made viable, and it is also the most reliable way to cause the run-out that loses it
edges.resolution_rule: run-out prevention wins at any account with an incident in the current review cycle; interval stretching is allowed only where the counted draw series shows headroom across the longer interval, and the first stretched cycle is verified at the next visit

edges.why_related: every added category earns more per stop and spends the route minutes that keep the service promises the whole book depends on
edges.resolution_rule: capacity wins: an expansion whose estimated added minutes would consume the stated slack is staged across cycles, re-sequenced onto a lighter route day, or deferred until capacity is added, and never launched on the assumption that the minutes will be found

edges.why_related: releasing a thin stop is right for that stop and can strand the neighbouring stops that shared its trip
edges.resolution_rule: run the incremental test in reverse before executing a release; if the stop is the anchor of its cluster, exhaust repricing and re-cadencing first, and if it still fails, plan the cluster's exit or replacement as one decision rather than releasing the anchor alone

edges.why_related: repeated run-outs are the most common avoidable path from a well-priced account to a cancellation, because they push the client into buying retail and comparing
the departure of the breakroom champion is what turns several health signals at once, from unanswered contact to sudden requests for itemized pricing
density buys back drive minutes, which is what makes a fast response and a tight interval affordable to promise in the first place
the small-stop instruments are chosen only after the fork has placed the stop on the volume branch, since a time-branch stop is made worse by a minimum
the credit is decided after the failure has been acknowledged, restored and verified, so that the giveaway settles a known cost rather than substituting for the fix
the review's input self-audit is what keeps counted draw and dated timings from decaying between cycles, feeding measurement quality back upstream
recovery runs consume the slack the promises were sized against, so a period of failures must feed back into what may be promised next
both are incident-driven trust loops with the same shape - record, root-cause, restore, verify, charge the cost to the stop - and they share the same failure of being handled informally and forgotten

conflict_axes.name: measured_contribution_vs_relationship_loyalty
conflict_axes.description: The stop the numbers say to release is often the account that has been loyal for years, refers other tenants and treats the driver like staff; the ledger and the relationship give opposite instructions.
poles: release or reprice on measured contribution
hold the account for its relationship and referral value
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: make the relationship value explicit and testable - name the referrals it has actually produced and the doors it actually opens - and if it cannot be named, the contribution decides

conflict_axes.name: price_integrity_vs_fear_of_losing_the_account
conflict_axes.description: An honest, evidenced increase is exactly the moment a client is most receptive to a competitor's tasting visit, so the operator is tempted into stealth methods or into absorbing costs indefinitely.
poles: disclose the increase and its cause in writing
protect the account by absorbing or by quiet adjustment
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclosure is not negotiable; the room to move is in the alternatives offered and the timing relative to service history, never in concealment

conflict_axes.name: stock_certainty_vs_client_inventory_burden
conflict_axes.description: The surest way to prevent a run-out is to leave more product on site, and the surest way to make a client feel over-sold is to leave more product on site.
poles: carry more stock at the account to eliminate run-outs
hold stock to measured draw and accept a thinner buffer
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prevent run-outs by fixing the cause the incident record names - interval, order tracking, shrink or an unannounced change - and treat added client-side stock as the last resort, agreed with the client rather than delivered into their cupboard

conflict_axes.name: service_richness_vs_route_minutes
conflict_axes.description: Everything clients love - a chat, a deeper clean, an extra check of the water system, a same-day response - is spent from the same finite pool of route-day minutes that determines whether the whole book gets served.
poles: give each account the service that delights it
protect the route day's committed and slack minutes
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: richness is allocated deliberately to the stops whose contribution and strategic value carry it, and the slack allowance is never the source it is drawn from

conflict_axes.name: expansion_revenue_vs_operational_simplicity
conflict_axes.description: Each new category raises revenue per stop and drags in spoilage, date codes, shrink, fixtures, freight weight and new obligation classes that the coffee route was never built to carry.
poles: grow revenue per stop through new categories
keep the route simple, fast and reliable
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: climb the ladder in order and require each step to be operating cleanly before the next is attempted, judging every candidate first on the minutes it adds to every visit

conflict_axes.name: equipment_carry_inside_price_vs_shown_separately
conflict_axes.description: Recovering the placed machine inside the product price is familiar and easy to sell but penalizes light users and makes increases look arbitrary; showing it separately is honest and invites line-by-line shopping.
poles: recover equipment and service cost inside the product price
show carry and service as their own disclosed components
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: whichever structure is chosen must be fully disclosable on request and applied consistently across accounts, so that no client discovers a cost they were never told about

conflict_axes.name: save_the_account_vs_concession_creep
conflict_axes.description: Every individual retention gesture is defensible in the moment, and their accumulation is an undisclosed permanent discount that no one ever decided to give.
poles: concede now to hold the account
hold the price and risk the cancellation
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: every concession carries a landed value, an owner and an end date, and the cumulative load at the stop is reviewed as if it were a price the operator had agreed deliberately

conflict_axes.name: density_discipline_vs_book_concentration
conflict_axes.description: Packing stops tightly is what makes the route profitable, and it is also what makes one building, campus or employer able to take a large share of the book away in a single decision.
poles: maximize density in the strongest clusters
spread exposure across buildings and employers
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: grow density inside a cluster until the concentration ceiling the operator has stated in advance is approached, then deliberately open or deepen a second cluster

conflict_axes.name: responsiveness_vs_sequence_integrity
conflict_axes.description: Breaking the loop to rescue one account is what earns a reputation for reliability, and doing it often is what destroys the reliability of everyone else's scheduled visit.
poles: respond immediately to the account in trouble
protect the planned sequence the other stops depend on
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: respond from the stated slack allowance, and when the slack is gone, offer a defined interim rather than a broken sequence, recording the event so the pattern becomes visible in capacity planning

conflict_axes.name: measurement_effort_vs_the_minutes_it_consumes
conflict_axes.description: Counting draw and timing visits is what makes every decision in this KB possible, and it is paid for in exactly the resource - stop minutes - that the whole analysis exists to protect.
poles: measure everything at every visit
measure lightly and decide on judgment
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: measure fully during a defined baseline period and at any account under review, and run a lighter standing count elsewhere, with the review's self-audit deciding where full measurement is reinstated

edge_cases.description: Single-serve pod counts climb steeply at an account whose headcount has not changed, and the operator reads it as adoption and raises the standing order
edge_cases.trigger: apparent draw rises with no occupancy or culture change to explain it
edge_cases.mitigation: investigate shrink before acting on the rise: compare the pattern across item classes, discuss access and storage with the client without accusing anyone, and hold the standing order until the cause is identified

edge_cases.description: An office moves to fewer in-office days and draw halves within two intervals while the same visit cadence continues
edge_cases.trigger: a hybrid or hoteling policy change at the account
edge_cases.mitigation: re-baseline draw against actual occupancy days, branch the stop on volume, and offer a longer interval or a consolidated order before any price conversation

edge_cases.description: A tenant relocates to an upper floor of the same building and the visit doubles in length because of freight-elevator scheduling
edge_cases.trigger: an internal move that leaves the account looking unchanged on paper
edge_cases.mitigation: re-time the stop across several visits, update the driver list with the new access constraint, and renegotiate the delivery point or the visit window with the client before repricing

edge_cases.description: A client asks to skip the next visit to save money but expects the breakroom to stay stocked, and runs out mid-week
edge_cases.trigger: a client-initiated schedule change without a matching order change
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm in writing what the skip means for quantities before agreeing to it, size the pre-skip order to the counted draw, and record the incident against the client-change cause if it still happens

edge_cases.description: Building management introduces new vendor badging, insurance documentation and dock booking that adds waiting time to every visit in the tower
edge_cases.trigger: a building policy change affecting several stops at once
edge_cases.mitigation: re-time all affected stops together, treat the cluster as one economic case rather than several, and decide on cluster-level repricing or re-cadencing before individual accounts are approached

edge_cases.description: A supplier increase lands while the account is inside a fixed-price term it agreed in writing
edge_cases.trigger: an input cost move that the agreement does not permit passing through yet
edge_cases.mitigation: absorb the move for the remaining term, log it with the date the term ends, prepare the evidenced notice for that date, and have the operator's own adviser review the term before assuming any earlier remedy exists

edge_cases.description: The office manager who has championed the service for years leaves, and the successor opens a competitive bid within weeks
edge_cases.trigger: champion departure detected late, often from a new signature on a delivery ticket
edge_cases.mitigation: respond with a factual re-introduction built from the account's own records - equipment, cadence, incident history, current pricing components - and treat the bid as a legitimate review rather than a betrayal

edge_cases.description: The largest account on the route demands a price concession and hints at consolidating all its buildings with one national vendor
edge_cases.trigger: a concentration-heavy account exercising its leverage
edge_cases.mitigation: compute what the account actually contributes and what the book looks like without it, decide the concession against that arithmetic rather than against fear, and start deliberate growth in a second cluster regardless of the outcome

edge_cases.description: A snack offering placed in a small office produces expired stock at the second review and the client asks to be credited for product nobody ate
edge_cases.trigger: a category launched into an account whose population cannot turn perishable stock
edge_cases.mitigation: credit the dated product without argument, withdraw or shrink the assortment to what the counted draw supports, and record the launch as a screening failure so the population and turn test is tightened

edge_cases.description: Micro-market losses jump after a headcount change and the client argues the shrink is the operator's problem
edge_cases.trigger: unattended-retail shrink exceeding what the qualification assumed, with no written loss terms in place
edge_cases.mitigation: return to the written loss terms if they exist and agree them now if they do not, adjust assortment and monitoring, and treat continued unbounded shrink as grounds to convert the market back to a serviced breakroom

edge_cases.description: The same brewer fails three times in one account, each time handled as a routine service call
edge_cases.trigger: repeat failures of one unit absorbed as individual tickets rather than escalated
edge_cases.mitigation: escalate the unit to a replacement decision on the recorded failure history, charge the accumulated recovery minutes and credits to the stop, and re-check the account's health signals for damage the tickets concealed

edge_cases.description: An account is comfortably profitable on paper while paying later every cycle and disputing invoice lines each month
edge_cases.trigger: a widening gap between billed contribution and cash actually collected at one stop
edge_cases.mitigation: surface payment behaviour and dispute frequency in the account's health state, resolve the invoicing cause if it is the operator's, and treat persistent non-payment as a release decision rather than a pricing one

workflow.action: Fix the stop as the unit of account and write the allocation rule
workflow.description: Decide what counts as one stop for every account on the route, including multi-floor tenants and shared suites, and state which costs attach to a stop and which are pooled and allocated by what rule
workflow.artifact: stop register with the split rule and the written route-cost allocation rule
workflow.gate: every serviced location maps to exactly one stop record, and the allocation rule is written and reproduces the same numbers on a re-run

workflow.action: Time the stops park to park across a run of visits
workflow.description: Capture measured minutes per visit with access, service, restock and client-conversation time separated, and hold drive minutes apart from stop minutes
workflow.artifact: minute ledger with dated observations per stop
workflow.gate: each stop carries multiple dated timings, access time is visible as its own category, and no drive minutes are charged directly to a stop

workflow.action: Start counting draw per item class at every account
workflow.description: Run the on-hand plus delivered minus remaining count each visit, normalize for interval length and occupancy, and separate shrink and waste from genuine consumption
workflow.artifact: draw series per account per item class with occupancy notes
workflow.gate: every account has counted intervals rather than inferred volumes, and any item class with an unexplained jump carries a shrink note

workflow.action: Record the cost-to-serve drivers per account
workflow.description: List the observed drivers behind each stop's minutes - access path, building requirements, delivery points, equipment class, water work, administrative drag - and tag who can change each
workflow.artifact: driver list per account with control tags
workflow.gate: each driver is an observed fact with a control tag, and the drivers named for a stop are consistent with its measured minutes

workflow.action: Compute stop contribution for every stop
workflow.description: Run the chain from billed revenue through landed product cost, loaded service labor, allocated drive and route cost, equipment carry and charged concessions to a contribution level and trend
workflow.artifact: per-stop contribution table with trend and stated bands where inputs are unmeasured
workflow.gate: every input names its source record, the loaded labor rate is documented and uniform, and unmeasured inputs appear as bands rather than point values

workflow.action: Fork every flagged stop on volume versus time
workflow.description: Assign each thin or negative stop to the volume branch or the time branch on measured evidence, and mark dual-failure stops for triage
workflow.artifact: diagnosis list with branch, evidence and licensed remedy set per stop
workflow.gate: no stop carries a remedy from outside its branch without a written exception, and dual-failure stops are routed to triage rather than to another repair

workflow.action: Rebuild the price architecture and the small-stop instruments
workflow.description: State the components each account's price is composed of, decide what is recovered inside product versus shown separately, and design the disclosed minimum, interval or consolidation instrument for stops that need one
workflow.artifact: price component sheet per account with any small-stop instrument and its compliance path
workflow.gate: components sum to the invoice with no unexplained residual, every component has a plain-language justification given in writing, and every instrument leaves the client a way to comply

workflow.action: Trace input-cost moves and decide absorb or pass through
workflow.description: Attach each documented supplier or freight move to the components and item classes it touches, and record the absorb-or-pass decision with a re-examination date
workflow.artifact: passthrough register with dated evidence per move
workflow.gate: no proposed change lacks a dated document and an affected-component mapping, and downward moves are reviewed on the same register

workflow.action: Run warranted increases through the disclosed reprice play
workflow.description: Check account health and service history, give written notice before the first affected delivery naming the moving input, and offer at least one genuine flat-spend alternative
workflow.artifact: notice pack per account with the alternative offered and its computed effect on contribution
workflow.gate: notice is dated before the affected delivery, no pack size or count is reduced without stating it, and no notice goes to an account with an unresolved service failure

workflow.action: Stand up the run-out and failure incident loops
workflow.description: Record every run-out and every service failure with cause, response and cost in minutes and credits, and route each to the prevention or recovery action its cause licenses
workflow.artifact: incident register with root causes and the prevention action taken
workflow.gate: each incident has a root cause and a matching action, repeat incidents are escalated, and no incident is closed by simply increasing the standing order

workflow.action: Build the account health state and its watch list
workflow.description: Combine draw trend, incident history, contact behaviour and billing signals into a per-account health state read against that account's own baseline, with an owner for each deteriorating account
workflow.artifact: health register with dated signals, states and assigned next actions
workflow.gate: every account has a current state with its evidence, and every deteriorating account has a named owner and a date

workflow.action: Gate and screen expansion, then review the route and book
workflow.description: Admit expansions only through the pull, reliability, sizing and disclosure conditions with obligation classes verified, then run the periodic review over draw, minutes, contribution, incidents, concessions, health, capacity and concentration, assigning one decision per flagged stop
workflow.artifact: review pack with the triage list, owners, dates and the input self-audit
workflow.gate: every flagged stop leaves with exactly one decision, an owner and a date; prior-cycle decisions are checked for outcome; and no expansion appears that lacks a pull signal or a completed obligation verification

priority_rationale: The measurement frame comes first because every later decision in route economics is an argument about a denominator: what counts as a stop, how many minutes it took, what actually left the cabinet and which costs belong to it. Contribution and the volume-versus-time diagnosis sit next, since no pricing, retention or expansion move can be chosen correctly until a stop's weakness has a cause. Pricing follows diagnosis so that increases are traced to documented input moves and disclosed to the client rather than engineered onto the invoice. Retention nodes - run-out economics, promise capacity, recovery, champion continuity and health signals - come before expansion because an operator who expands an unreliable account sells on top of a broken promise, and they feed the save-or-release decision. Expansion is gated on measured pull, screened on the minutes it adds, and blocked until the obligation classes it touches are locally verified. Route density, book value and the periodic review close the order, because they compose individual stop decisions into a route that can be served, a book that is not fragile, and a cycle that keeps the whole apparatus honest between reviews.

dominance_rules.rule: Verified local obligation classes dominate every category launch
dominance_rules.rationale: an unverified food, water, weights-and-measures or unattended-retail obligation is usually discovered by the client or the building, which costs the account as well as the category
dominance_rules.trigger: any proposal to add food, refrigeration, water equipment, posted-price selling or an unattended market at an account
dominance_rules.action: hold the launch until each applicable obligation class carries a dated written verification with the responsible authority in that jurisdiction

dominance_rules.rule: Measured consumption evidence dominates expansion revenue
dominance_rules.rationale: volume pushed into a client's cupboard converts goodwill into resentment and returns later as a cancellation that takes the coffee service with it
dominance_rules.trigger: any offer to increase quantity, assortment or category at an existing account
dominance_rules.action: require a dated pull signal from the account's own records and size the first order to counted draw with a stated review at the next visit

dominance_rules.rule: Route capacity dominates any service promise
dominance_rules.rationale: a missed promise costs more than the promise earned, because it converts the reliability story that holds the book into the complaint that loses it
dominance_rules.trigger: a client asks for a shorter interval, faster response or a fixed window, or a new stop is proposed on a full route day
dominance_rules.action: commit only inside available minutes with the slack allowance intact; otherwise re-shape, re-sequence, add capacity or say plainly what can be committed

dominance_rules.rationale: a client who discovers a shrunk pack or an unexplained fee stops believing every number the operator has ever given them, and the account is lost at the discovery rather than at the increase
dominance_rules.trigger: any price, pack, fee or surcharge change under consideration
dominance_rules.action: state the change and its cause in writing before it takes effect, or do not make it

dominance_rules.rule: Core reliability dominates expansion effort at the same account
dominance_rules.rationale: selling a new category on top of an unresolved run-out or an unfixed machine reads to the client as an operator who wants more money and cannot deliver what is already sold
dominance_rules.trigger: an expansion opportunity at an account with an open incident or an unverified fix
dominance_rules.action: close and verify the reliability issue first, then re-open the expansion conversation

dominance_rules.rule: Measured contribution dominates billed revenue in every triage decision
dominance_rules.rationale: the largest invoices on a route are routinely attached to the stops that consume the most minutes, so revenue ranking inverts the truth
dominance_rules.trigger: any decision to keep, reprice, re-cadence, expand or release a stop
dominance_rules.action: rank and decide on contribution computed through the stated chain, never on invoice size

dominance_rules.rule: Cash actually collected dominates paper contribution
dominance_rules.rationale: a stop that bills well, pays late and disputes monthly is consuming working capital and administrative time that no contribution figure shows
dominance_rules.trigger: an account whose payment behaviour or dispute frequency diverges from the rest of the book
dominance_rules.action: surface payment behaviour in the account's health state and treat persistent non-payment as a release decision rather than a pricing one

dominance_rules.rule: A sanitation or safety defect dominates the schedule
dominance_rules.rationale: serving from equipment that is unsafe or unsanitary risks the client's people and the operator's standing far beyond the value of the visit
dominance_rules.trigger: a brewer, water system or cooler found in a condition the operator would not drink from
dominance_rules.action: take the equipment out of service and provide an interim rather than completing the visit as scheduled

dominance_rules.rule: The client's own records dominate the operator's assumption in any consumption dispute
dominance_rules.rationale: the operator's credibility rests on being the one who counts rather than the one who estimates, and a disagreement settled on the client's own numbers ends permanently
dominance_rules.trigger: a client challenges quantities, frequency or the size of a standing order
dominance_rules.action: settle the question against the counted draw series and the client's own occupancy information, and adjust if the client is right

dominance_rules.rule: Cluster integrity dominates an individual release decision
dominance_rules.rationale: releasing the anchor stop of a distant cluster can turn its profitable neighbours into marginal ones overnight
dominance_rules.trigger: a release decision for a stop that shares its trip with other accounts
dominance_rules.action: run the incremental test in reverse and decide the cluster as one case before executing any release

anti_rework_rules.rule: Measure stop minutes and counted draw before choosing any remedy for a thin stop
anti_rework_rules.prevents: repricing an account whose problem was access time, or stretching the interval at an account whose problem was a growing draw

anti_rework_rules.rule: Separate shrink from genuine draw before increasing any standing order
anti_rework_rules.prevents: repeatedly raising quantities that keep disappearing, which raises cost, invites a run-out anyway and eventually becomes an uncomfortable conversation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Compute stop contribution before agreeing to a new cadence, a new category or a new promise
anti_rework_rules.prevents: committing route minutes to an account that cannot carry the visit it already receives

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify the applicable obligation classes before ordering fixtures, coolers or refrigerated stock
anti_rework_rules.prevents: sunk investment in a category that has to be stood down, and the loss of client confidence that stand-down causes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Resolve and verify open reliability issues before making any expansion offer at that account
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an expansion conversation that hardens an unhappy client's decision to look at competitors

anti_rework_rules.rule: Put the price architecture and any minimum in writing before the first invoice under it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a dispute in which the operator has to reconstruct after the fact what the client was supposed to have agreed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the incremental minutes test before signing an out-of-cluster stop
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a route day quietly stretched past its slack, which surfaces later as missed visits across accounts that had nothing to do with the new one

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record equipment serial, condition, placement terms and the recovery path at installation and keep it current
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an exit in which the operator cannot identify, locate or recover a machine, or has to argue about its condition

anti_rework_rules.rule: Identify a second contact at every account while the champion is still there
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering a champion's departure from a cancellation email and having to re-justify the whole service to a stranger

anti_rework_rules.rule: Agree the measurement basis with the client before repricing anything that depends on consumption
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an increase that collapses into an argument about whose numbers are right at the worst possible moment

iteration_protocol.trigger: measured draw at an account moves outside its established band for more than one interval
iteration_protocol.action: re-baseline against occupancy, investigate shrink, then adjust order size and interval before touching price

iteration_protocol.trigger: a supplier, freight or labor input cost moves and is documented
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the passthrough trace, decide absorb or pass through per account with a re-examination date, and run warranted increases through the disclosed play

iteration_protocol.trigger: a second run-out or a repeat service failure at the same account within a review cycle
iteration_protocol.action: escalate from incident handling to a root-cause review of interval, order tracking, shrink and equipment, and re-check what has been promised against capacity

iteration_protocol.trigger: the named champion at an account changes, or the approval process changes
iteration_protocol.action: run the factual re-introduction from the account's own records, re-establish an alternate contact, and re-read the health signals that the change may have masked

iteration_protocol.trigger: a stop is added, released or re-timed on a route day
iteration_protocol.action: recompute incremental minutes and the day's remaining slack, re-check cluster anchors, and update what may be promised on that day

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new category has completed its first full cycle at an account
iteration_protocol.action: recompute the stop's contribution including spoilage, shrink and added minutes, compare against what the screen assumed, and shrink, grow or withdraw the assortment accordingly

iteration_protocol.trigger: the share of book contribution held by one account, building or employer approaches the stated ceiling
iteration_protocol.action: open or deepen a second cluster deliberately and re-examine any concession being granted to the dominant account

iteration_protocol.trigger: the periodic review cycle falls due, or a cycle is skipped
iteration_protocol.action: run the full review over the standing input set with its self-audit, check prior decisions for outcome, and assign exactly one owned, dated decision per flagged stop
